topics.title: AMC 8 Prep Problem 2
topics.text:
Significantly harder; around #25 level, so proceed with care.



Suppose $f(n)$ denotes the value obtained when the positive integer $n$ is raised to itself a total of $n$ times.

By standard convention, highest exponents are computed first, working downward, so that $a^{b^c}=a^{(b^c)}$. For example, $f(1)=1$, $f(2)=2^2=4$, and $f(3)=3^{3^3}=3^{27}$. Armed with this information, what is the units digit of $f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+...+f(2018)$?



Search the "amc8prepfun" tag for more.

topics.title: Fun Quick Problem
topics.text:
There are 1000 people in line for a certain game.



In this game, there are 1000 cups face down on a table, with just one cup that has exactly 1000 dollars under it. None of the other cups have anything under them. You get to choose one of the cups. You win by choosing the cup with money under it. If you win, you take the entirety of the 1000 dollars and everyone behind you in line doesn't get to play. If you lose, you take the cup that you picked and the people behind you repeat the process.



The person in the $n$th spot in line at the very beginning has the highest expected payoff. Find $n$.



Extensions:



How would the answer change if you had to pay a fee of 1 cent right before playing the game? What about 5 cents? 25 cents? A dollar? 5 dollars? 20 dollars?

topics.title: Variable Expression Problem - What's the error n.28
topics.text:
NOTE: My english is translated by google. Sorry for incogruence.



Problem:

A student says $3(n-5)$ is equal to $3n - 5$. What's the error?



Solution:

We place

$ 3 (n-5) = 3n-5  $

$ = 3n-15 = 3n-5  $

$ = 3n-3n-15 = 3n-3n-5  $

$ = - 15 \neq -5$

so the two expressions are not the same.

The error is that $3n - 3*5 \neq 3n-5$

topics.title: 2018 MS MTE Theme Round (All)
topics.text:
1. Who needs Vieta's?

If $ r $ and $ s $ are the roots of $ x^2 + 6x + 8 $, find $ \dfrac{4}{r} + \dfrac{4}{s} $.



2. Add 'em up!

Given that $ \dfrac{3 - 2x}{4x^2 + 8x + 3} = \dfrac{2}{2x + 1} - \dfrac{3}{2x + 3} $, evaluate $$ \sum_{k = 1}^{3} \dfrac{3 - 2k}{4k^2 + 8k + 3} $$

3. Comparing squares and cubics

Jill has two geometric sequences. Both sequences have 3 consecutive terms. If the first sequence is

$(1, x-1, x^3-12x^2+42x-31)$, and the second sequence is $(1, x-2, x^3-11x^2+32x-28)$, what is the value of $x$?



4. Divide through and you're done

Find the sum of the coefficients of the polynomial $$ \frac{264x^3+792x^2+528x}{\left( \frac{4! \cdot 6!}{720} \right)} $$

5. Use the factorization, Luke

Consider the polynomial $$ f(x) = 4x^3 - 48x^2 + 189x - 243 $$with inverse $ g $. Given that $ g(0) = 3 $, and that $ f $ has a double root, what is the sum of the distinct roots of $ f $?



6. Tying your shoes has never been harder

A triangle in the Cartesian plane has coordinates $ (x, 2), (18, 3x), (6, 5x) $. If $ \left| p(x) \right| $ is the expression that yields the triangle's area for all real numbers $ x $, then what is the sum of the coefficients of $ p(x) $?



7. I'll solve your conditional probability problem...under one condition!

Three integers are randomly chosen from the interval $ [-1, 1] $. What is the probability that these three integers are the roots of the polynomial $$ x^3 + ax^2 + bx + c $$for $ a, c \in [0, 1] $?



8. Elegant powers of two

Given the polynomial $ P(x) = x^3+2x^2+4x+8 $ with roots $ a $, $ b $, and $ c $, find $ \dfrac{1}{a} + \dfrac{1}{b} + \dfrac{1}{c} $.



9. Square and subtract two

If eighteen times $ x $ minus 1 is equal to the square of $ x $, what is the units digit of $ x^{2048} + x^{-2048} $?



10. Paper cuts are bad

Joe has a paper rectangle with side lengths $ x $ and $ y $, where $ x, y > 4 $. He cuts out a $ 2 \times 2 $ square from each corner, then folds the sides of the box upward. Finally, he closes the top with another rectangle. If the volume of the new shape is $ 216 $ $ \text{units}^3 $, how many ordered pairs $ (x, y) $ are possible?



11. Is this prism even possible?

Let $ p $, $ q $, and $ r $ be the roots of the polynomial $ x^3 + 20x^2 + 18x - 2018 $. If $ p $, $ q $, and $ r $ are the side lengths of a rectangular prism, what is the ratio of the volume to the surface area of that prism?



12. A more convoluted Triangle Inequality

Let $ a, b, c $ be the integer side lengths of a scalene triangle, with $ a $, $ b $, and $ c $ not all being consecutive. Given that $ c $ is the largest of the side lengths, and that $ x = a + b - 2c $ is a root of the polynomial $ f(x) = x^2 + k $, where $ k $ is a constant, what is the largest possible value of $ k $?



13. The induction of bridge-builders

Let $ P(x) = (x  -3)(x - 9) $. Let there exist a function $ G(x) $ where $ G(1) = P(x) $, $ G(2) = P(P(x)) $, $ G(3) = P(P(P(x))) $, and so forth. What is the sum of the roots of $ G(10) $?



14. The coefficients that distract you

Let $ f(x) = 2x^5+x^4-26x^3-13x^2+72x+36 $. A new polynomial is defined by $ g(x) = f(x+4) $. Find the sum of the roots of the equation $ g(x) = 0 $.



15. Woefully short

If $ r, s, t $ are the roots of $ 2x^3 + 10x + 8 $, then determine $ r^2 + rs + rt + s^2 + st + t^2 $.

topics.title: Very ez problem
topics.text:
Here is an extremely easy problem that I came up with in the car because I was bored:

How many numbers $n \in{\mathbb{N}}$ exist such that $\left[\frac{n}{7}\right]=\lceil \frac{n}{7} \rceil$ and $n <100$



Here $[x]$ denotes the closest positive integer of $x$. For example $[5]=5$ and $[5.3]=5$ and $[6.7]=7$



Also $\lceil x \rceil$ denotes the least integer greater than or equal to $x$. For example $\lceil 10.3 \rceil =11$ and $\lceil 13.7 \rceil =14$

topics.title: Spooky Random-Walk - OMG Hallorachnid Alert: Halloween Edition
topics.text:
As you all probably know, a spider is an arachnid. A super rare type of arachnid is called a hallorachnid, something that can move swiftly and attack incoming prey during the night of Halloween. :evilgrin:



I am standing at the apex of a tetrahedral mountain to meet up with my cousins for Halloween when I, all of a sudden, see a hallorachnid standing at a vertex of the mountain. Unfortunately, right then, a wind storm occurs, rendering me and the hallorachnid unable to see. Therefore, because I am scared, I decide to perform a vertex-to-vertex random walk  :whistling: (uhhhhh I don't want to die...). The hallorachnid, also helpless, decides to do the same. Every minute, the hallorachnid and I make it to a different emanating vertex of the tetrahedral mountain. As soon as I reach the same vertex as it does, I immediately die. :wacko:



If the wind storm lasts an infinite amount of time, please help me figure out the expected number of minutes I have left to live before I die upon attack! In case you don't know what a tetrahedron is, it is a pyramid with a triangular base.



Challenge from me to you :)



For more, search the "spooky problems" tag.

You are allowed to use a calculator.

topics.title: AoPS edition problems
topics.text:
Here are some AoPS edition problems I made.



1. Find the number of permutations of the word AOPS.



2. If $a+o+p=3$, $a+o+s=-15$, $a+p+s=1$, and $o+p+s=17$, what is the product $aops$?



3. Richard the AoPSer has 100 AoPS posts in total. However, only 30 of them are "official" (posts from forums like Fun Factory and Accumulation Playoffs don't count as "official"). If he has 15 posts on Middle School Math, 10 posts on High School Math, 5 posts on Contests and Programs, 35 posts on Fun Factory, and 35 posts on Accumulation Playoffs, what is the probability that 3 randomly selected posts will all be in different forums and will all count as "official"?



4. How many default AoPS avatar color-combos are possible assuming that you must choose 3 distinct colors from 16 different colors, and red and blue can't be used on the same avatar? (If two avatars with the same color combo have a different orientation (e.g. yellow is on the top instead of on the side), they are still counted as the same.)



5. The letters 'A', 'O', 'P', and 'S' are randomly placed on four of the eight vertices on a cube. How many different arrangements are possible if rotations of arrangements are considered the same?



6. Three people log in to AoPS at a random time between 9pm and 11pm. All three people stay on AoPS for exactly 30 minutes and then log out. Find the probability that at least two of the three people will be online at the same time.
